newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bonino says world indifferent, racist over Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Bonino says world indifferent, racist over Zaire.

text.p: Emma Bonino, the European Union's humanitarian aid Commissioner accused the world community on Thursday of indifference bordering on racism over the plight of 700,000 refugees still stranded in eastern Zaire.

"How many lives have to be in danger, how many people missing to justify a deployment of troops by the "civilised world'? Who sets the threshold -- is it 500,000, 200,000, 100,000 or 10,000," she said at the European Parliament.
"Is it the colour of their skin which makes the difference, which leads us to believe that it is their inevitable lot to be linked to a cycle of...massacres."

Bonino said a proposed U.N. multinational force, now in doubt, was essential to allow humanitarian aid workers to save lives in Zaire. Without that protection, aid workers risked being killed and taken hostage, she said.

The United Nations said on Thursday it had sent an assessment team into Zaire's Bukavu to track down up to 700,000 missing Rwandan Hutu refugees, which are central to the debate over planned military intervention.

Troop contributors are scheduled to meet on Friday in the German city of Stuttgart to evaluate the lastest situation after 500,000 refugees unexpectedly returned to Rwanda last week to flee fighting between Zairean rebels and soldiers from Rwanda's Hutu-dominated former army and Hutu militias.

The U.N.'s World Food Programme said on Thursday as many as 100,000 Hutu refugees were on the road again, possibly signalling the start of a second mass exodus to their homeland and further weakening international will to intervene.
"An intervention was considered justified for 1.2 million refugees -- and now they say 'things have changed!' Is that what you call the civilised world?" Bonino said. "Where are the rest?"
Bonino, the most vocal critic of the U.N. Security Council for its slowness in reacting to the crisis in Zaire, said the situation made a mockery of the European Union's foreign and security policy.
"Can we defend foreign policies solely based on national interests?" she said.
In an interview with Christian RCF radio in Paris, Bonino accused the United States of delaying a decision to send troops to Zaire in the hope that the crisis would work itself out.
"They don't want an intervention. I get the feeling they had won their bet from the very start," she told the radio.

"They took their time, and in doing so, the (Tutsi) rebels did the work the multinational force should have done in a more ordered way: they bombed (the Mugunga camp), just as they bombed the other camps," Bonino said.
